issues.legal_issue: A widow who acquires premises with an existing tenant cannot use the special immediate-eviction procedure when the premises were let by neither her nor her husband.
material_facts: The tenant’s predecessor had occupied the premises as a tenant under the former owner before the widow acquired the premises by purchase.
The widow sought eviction through the special procedure for a widow, claiming that she required the premises for her own residence.
The widow had not let the premises, and her husband had not let them.
issues.conclusion: The widow was not entitled to invoke the special immediate-eviction procedure. The appeal was allowed, the eviction orders were set aside, and her eviction application was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The special provisions for immediate recovery are exceptions to the tenant-protective scheme and must be applied according to their stated conditions. The words requiring that the premises have been let by the widow or her husband must be given their ordinary meaning; they cannot be omitted or treated as redundant. The widow’s special right therefore extends only to premises let by her or her husband, not premises let by another person merely because she later became the landlord. This reading gives effect to all the words used and harmonizes the widow-specific provision with the restriction on a transferee landlord’s recovery of possession. The Court preferred Surjit Singh Kalra v. Union of India and distinguished Kanta Goel v. B.P. Pathak, whose relevant observations were not necessary to its decision. The Court also relied on the principles of statutory interpretation stated in State of U.P. v. Vijay Anand Maharaj; Rananjaya Singh v. Baijnath Singh; Kanai Lal Sur v. Paramnidhi Sadhukhan; Nyadar Singh v. Union of India; J.K. Cotton Spinning and Weaving Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of U.P.; Ghanshyam Das v. Regional Assistant Commissioner, Sales Tax; Nasiruddin v. Sita Ram Agarwal; Swedish Match AB v. Securities & Exchange Board, India; High Court of Gujarat v. Gujarat Kishan Mazdoor Panchayat; Imdad Ali v. Keshav Chand; and Balwant Singh v. Anand Kumar Sharma. The relevant provisions were Sections 14(6), 14B, 14C and 14D of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, with the special eviction procedure under Section 25B.

predicates.widow_seeks_immediate_residence_possessi: A widow seeks possession of rented premises for her own residence.
predicates.special_widow_eviction_proceeding: The landlord brings a proceeding that provides a widow with a special route to immediate eviction.
predicates.premises_let_by_another_person: A person other than the widow or her husband let the premises to the tenant.
predicates.widow_acquired_premises_with_existing_te: The widow acquired the premises after the tenant was already occupying them under the former landlord.

issues.definition: When a widow seeks immediate possession for her residence through the special eviction proceeding, but another person let the premises and she acquired them with the tenant already in place, the special immediate-eviction route is unavailable.
